title: demo-profile moves to behaviour-style source and pins one evaluator per Production cluster
notes: Two changes in one release because they have to land together: demo-profile switches to behaviour-style source, where every flag sits in its own named function at a real call site, and its single Production evaluator is replaced by one per cluster.

Behaviour style is what makes the removal pull request readable. A flag leaving an array is one line of noise; a flag leaving this source deletes a function, deletes a registry line, and adds a comment recording that the behaviour is now permanent.

Cluster pinning is what makes the drain visible. Five evaluators each pinned to one Production cluster can run different release tags at the same time, so a code removal rolled out cluster by cluster shows up as steps rather than as a cliff.

Evaluators go from eight to twelve. Dated 1 September on purpose: the metered month resets first, so this spends a fresh budget rather than the last quarter of August. Re-measure after a full day before going further.

demo-legacy-profile is the subject because demo-profile is its only consumer. A flag with a second live caller can never reach zero evaluations, which is the trap this whole talk is about; here the drain can actually complete.
